title: 2021 HMMT November Guts Problem 5
statement: A perfect power is an integer \(n\) that can be represented as \(a^{k}\) for some positive integers \(a \geq 1\) and \(k \geq 2\). Find the sum of all prime numbers \(0<p<50\) such that \(p\) is 1 less than a perfect power.

solutions.text: First, it is known that \(a^{k}-1=(a-1)\left(a^{k-1}+a^{k-2}+\ldots\right)\). This means either \(a-1\) or \(a^{k-1}+a^{k-2}+\ldots+1\) must be 1 in order for \(a^{k}-1\) to be prime. But this only occurs when \(a\) is 2 . Thus, the only possible primes are of the form \(2^{k}-1\) for some integer \(k>1\). One can check that the primes of this form less than 50 are \(2^{2}-1=3,2^{3}-1=7\), and \(2^{5}-1=31\).
